topic: Perioperative management of RA: holding DMARDs and biologics for surgery
synopsis: This review summarizes perioperative guidance for rheumatoid arthritis, including the ACR/American Association of Hip and Knee Surgeons recommendations for elective hip or knee arthroplasty. Conventional DMARDs—methotrexate, leflunomide, sulfasalazine, and hydroxychloroquine—are continued through the perioperative period. The rationale cited is a low infection risk with methotrexate outside surgery and small randomized trials in which stopping conventional DMARDs before surgery produced a similar or higher postoperative infection risk. Biologics are held for one dosing interval before surgery, using the dosing interval rather than the half-life because half-life was thought to match duration of action less well. Worked examples are infliximab every 8 weeks, last dose 9 weeks before surgery, and adalimumab every 2 weeks, last dose 3 weeks before surgery.
